reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the presenter urges viewers to buy Tycoon packs and describes card or wire payments to participate in a mining pool, linking those payments to claims of at least fivefold first-year returns and large profit projections. The presentation also promotes network bonuses, while its profit amounts are framed as projections rather than realized returns.

opening.argument: Judge, the presenter does not present the price path as an observed return. He calls the profit figures projections, and the price chart explicitly disclaims certainty about whether its values will be reached. He also warns that some cryptocurrencies may be fake. Those qualifications matter: a forecast about a speculative market, even an optimistic one, is different from evidence that viewers are promised a guaranteed payout.

citations.quote: As a tycoon, you can make €30,000 to €45,000 profit based upon projections.
you have to be careful, there's some fakes out there as well

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited payment and mining-slot language establishes how someone could participate, but not that a return is guaranteed or has already been paid. The network-income statement likewise describes a second opportunity; it does not erase the explicit qualification that the profit figures are projections. The chart asks viewers to consider scenarios, not a verified payout history.

citations.quote: based upon projections

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling figures projections does not neutralize the sales pitch. The presenter says buyers will get at least five times their money in the first year, links the result to recruiting growth, and urges purchases of the highest-tier packs. The disclaimer does not change the central offer: pay into packages, obtain mining slots, and expect substantial returns.

citations.quote: At the very minimum, you're getting five times your money in the first year.
Well, frankly, I would buy as many tycoon packs as I could afford.
use them to purchase your slots in the mining pools

opening.argument: Judge, substantial time is spent walking through an educational program and its tools. The presenter describes training levels, quizzes, and a threshold for progressing, then explains how members can use an internal exchange. He even says the training is not mandatory for someone interested only in buying and selling. That is meaningful operational instruction, not merely a demand to send money; the viewer is shown what the program teaches and how its interface works.

rebuttal.rebuttal: A payment method does not tell us the entire purpose of the webinar. The presenter identifies education packages and explains their training levels and exchange interface. Nor does the cited mining-slot phrase establish that the instructional material is fictitious. The network opportunity is discussed, but it is not the only activity described.

just showing you actually uh the different training levels
So the One Exchange is our internal trading platform.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The instructional material serves the paid mining offer. The presenter says package tokens buy mining-pool positions, urges members to accumulate tokens for more coins, and explicitly describes mining-linked capital growth as where they will make their big money. Demonstrating a dashboard does not make that earnings pitch an ordinary tutorial.

citations.quote: the products we sell, the packages, our education packages, we actually also give you some free items in those packages, one of which are called tokens.
You can use the tokens, however, to buy slots or buy your positions in the mining pools.

opening.argument: Judge, the identifiable purchase is an education package with tokens included, not a request for credentials or a bare transfer in exchange for a guaranteed payout. The description invites people to register for free, study, and ask questions. The presenter describes the training as optional and says his long-term figures do not require sponsoring anyone. Those details support reading this as promotion of a paid service with optional trading and referral features, rather than treating every package purchase as proof of a deceptive mechanism.

For an introduction, you can register for free, study, and ask questions.
Of course, it's not mandatory.
By the way, this is without sponsoring anyone. This is just on your pack alone.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The payment quote shows a purchase option, not a guaranteed return or a credential request. Mining slots and network bonuses are described, but the presenter also identifies education packages and says the cited pack-only profits do not depend on recruitment. The prosecution's examples establish an aggressive commercial offer; they do not, by themselves, establish that education is absent or that every participant must build a downline.

citations.quote: the products we sell, the packages, our education packages
By the way, this is without sponsoring anyone. This is just on your pack alone.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Recruitment need not be mandatory for the paid-mining pitch to be concerning. The presenter says packages supply tokens, tokens buy mining-pool slots, and more tokens generate more coins. He then recommends buying as many Tycoon packs as one can afford and presents large projected profits without sponsoring. Calling the purchase education does not remove that pay-to-participate earnings mechanism.
